claims.text: Liminal Coil stays in the main hand on every rung: it grants Coiling Bolts and both per-curse gains, so the wand can't be swapped out for a stat stick. Its "Magnitudes of Curses you inflict are zero" also means the curses slow and weaken nothing: each one only counts on the target.

The clear assumes Windscream's "Curses have no Activation Delay" reaches Blasphemy's curses. That is the user's guess: the line names no aura, no lookup settles it, and PoB's figures don't move on it, so it needs in-game testing. If it doesn't reach them, each pack waits out the curses' 1.5 second delay uncursed, at less than half the hit and with no chain.

source.ref: the user's guess at the brainstorm gate; lookup_game_data unique "Windscream" and gem "Temporal Chains"; the card's condition check, Blasphemy's group off at about two fifths of the figure

claims.text: m's curse gems are level 17, and a level 17 curse doesn't apply to enemies above level 78, but the wand's Hedgewitch Assandra's Rune of Wisdom gives +1 to Level of all Spell Skills, so m's curses run at skill level 18, whose row has no cap. The cap only bites on a wand without the rune: there, above level 78, the curses, the per-curse gains and the chain all stop together. With the rune socketed, the level 18 gems at character level 78 are no deadline. The cap comes from the gems' level table: PoB doesn't measure what it does in play.

source.ref: Data/Skills/act_int.lua:5306-5307; lookup_game_data gem "Temporal Chains" at gem levels 17 and 18; lookup_game_data mechanic "to Level of all Spell Skills" kind mod, Hedgewitch Assandra's Rune of Wisdom (wand); m's Weapon 1; m.g2s3p1.ManaCost 184, skill level 18's 160 × 1.15 with Overzealous

claims.text: With Mind Over Matter off, m's regeneration beats Necromantic Conduit's 5% drain by about 14 mana a second, so mana stays full with no flask and Unholy Might stays up.

Don't take Mind Over Matter on any rung: its 50% less mana recovery would put m's regeneration under Necromantic Conduit's drain, and from full, mana would reach Low Mana in about 43 seconds with no flask and no hit taken.
Losing Unholy Might at Low Mana costs m about 8% of its map figure, which is what keeping mana over Low Mana is worth on this rung.

m's toughness fell at the design gate's revision. Taking Mind Over Matter off, as the user asked, took EHP from 5,874 to 4,682 and lowest max hit from 3,418 to 2,699, and energy shield stayed 1,630, since the tree rebuild that would have moved its points into energy shield was illegal on Dexterity. Damage rose about 1%.

source.ref: the first design gate's m rung, reports/gates/D1-gate-r1-s-4-a1.json (EHP 5,874, 166,193) against this plan's compile, m.TotalEHP, m.EnergyShield (4,682, 1,630, 167,952); the 3,418, the 2,699 and the rebuild's Dexterity failure as the design revision reported them

claims.text: Event Horizon stays off every tree, as the user ruled at the design gate. PoB reads its 53% increased Chaos Damage but not its loss of 3% of maximum life and energy shield on each chaos cast, and the build regenerates no life: at n's cast speed that empties life in about 12 seconds.

Coiling Bolts is the boss skill too: it has no cooldown or charge and PoB lists no mana cost, unconfirmed in game, so a boss fight is the same button as a pack, standing inside the curse aura. Withering Presence's stacks ramp the same skill, and on b and n Attrition does too.

source.ref: lookup_game_data gem "Coiling Bolts" (1-20: Cost 0 Mana, no cooldown row); m.g1s1p2.ManaCost

claims.text: Ascendancy order on m: Energy Shield, Eldritch Empowerment, Mana, Necromantic Conduit, Curse Area, Rupture the Soul. Eldritch Empowerment comes first for 30% more on every cast, with Energy Shield on the way to it; Mana leads to Necromantic Conduit, whose Unholy Might adds a share of the hit as chaos; Curse Area widens the aura, which lengthens the chain; Rupture the Soul comes last, since its explosions only help once packs die to the chain.

The tree keeps Efficient Inscriptions and Zone of Control. Efficient Inscriptions' 20% increased Reservation Efficiency for Meta Skills is what lets Blasphemy hold five curses on this Spirit, and node power sees no damage from Spirit that is merely reserved. Zone of Control's 20% increased Area of Effect of Curses widens the aura the chain runs in, and PoB has no chain count, so node power can't see that either.

Buy m in this order: Liminal Coil, since nothing works without it; Threaded Light with its two runes; Alpha's Howl, for the Spirit that pays the fifth curse; Windscream; Veilpiercer and Grip of Kulemak; then the resistance rares, amulet, body armour, belt and gloves. The ten slots come to about 4.05 divines as seen on 2026-11-01, under the 5-divine target before any conversion to day 7.

source.ref: the order follows the card's chain and the slots' prices, m-weapon1 to m-ring2, 2026-11-01

Act 4, Eye of Hinekora, Tribal Medicine: take 30% increased Global Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield, since energy shield is the pool.
Act 4, Halls of the Dead, Tawhoa's Test: take +5% to Lightning Resistance, which frees a rare's suffix from the cap.
Act 4, Halls of the Dead, Tasalio's Test: take +5% to Cold Resistance, which frees a rare's suffix from the cap.

claims.text: Wildshards II stays out on every rung: PoB reads nothing of it, and inside the aura the chain already reaches every cursed monster. Sione's Temper is its gem family at a Lineage gem's price, so it stays out with it.

source.ref: pieces.md rows i1b-13 and i1a-18; the card's dead-slot audit

claims.text: Incessant Cacophony and hand-cast curses stay out on every rung: five curses fit Blasphemy through Alpha's Howl and Efficient Inscriptions, so nothing is cast by hand for the node to hold, and a curse in Blasphemy can't also be cast by hand.

Spell crit stays unpulled: Coiling Bolts' base crit chance is 7%, which would need about 170% increased crit chance to match Controlled Destruction's 25% more Hit Damage, and that support forbids crits, so the compiled crit chance reads 0.

source.ref: pieces.md's search Q21; lookup_game_data gem "Controlled Destruction"; b.g1s1p2.CritChance

claims.text: Shock and exposure stay unpulled: the hits are physical and chaos, so neither has anything to scale, and Frost Bomb's Elemental Exposure stays out for the same reason.
Curse effect stays unpulled: the wand sets every curse you inflict to zero magnitude, so nothing that raises a curse's magnitude can reach the hit. The curses pay through their count alone.

Sigil of Power and Archmage stay unpulled, with Mana Tempest: the first reads mana spent, the second puts a cost on a spell that has none, and the third empowers mana-costing spells, while the bolts' compiled mana cost reads 0.

PoB's first choice for the fifth support is Deliberation's 20% more Damage; the build takes Mobility. Deliberation's 30% more movement penalty leaves 9% of walking speed while casting, Mobility's 25% less penalty leaves 47.5%, and PoB's damage figure can't weigh a build that casts on the move.

On b and n the build takes Rapid Casting II over Considered Casting, whose 35% more Damage at 15% less Cast Speed reads about the same figure. One or two casts already kill a normal pack, so shorter stops are worth more than a bigger hit, which PoB's damage figure doesn't weigh.

source.ref: lookup_game_data gem "Rapid Casting II"; gem "Considered Casting"

claims.text: Blackened Heart stays out: it read +3.3%, against the energy shield and curse area the same two ascendancy points buy.
Eternal Life stays out: the notables taken feed the hit, the explosion and Unholy Might, and a fifth gives up the energy shield and curse area points.
Price of Power stays out: nothing in the build makes Power Charges for it to consume.
Apep's Supremacy stays out: the focus slot holds Threaded Light, and its poison is one stack, a small slice on a fast hit.
Atziri's Communion stays out: it costs about 40% of life a curse, and Spirit no longer falls short.
Immaculate Adherence stays out: its "Cannot have Energy Shield" ends Eldritch Empowerment's sacrifice.
Snakepit stays out: its left slot forbids chains, and its right slot's one chain adds nothing to a chain with no count.
Spark and Fireball stay out: neither chains through cursed targets, so either gives up the build's reach.

claims.text: b's tree keeps Efficient Inscriptions and Zone of Control. Efficient Inscriptions pays for the five curses, whose Spirit node power doesn't count as damage, and Zone of Control widens the aura the chain runs in, which PoB has no chain count to measure.

Buy b in this order from m: the wand copy with its corruption, Threaded Light at 11%, Grip of Kulemak and Windscream's better roll, all under a divine; then Morior Invictus at 14 divines with its five runes, which moves EHP most; the gloves, the belt and Alpha's Howl's two-socket copy, about 3 divines each as seen; the amulet at 5; Heart of the Well and the sapphires at 1, 2 and 5; the anoint last. The two trades at the design gate, Against the Darkness and a +3 levels amulet, are upgrades past this budget.

b's tree keeps Profane Commander for its 4% increased Spirit: Spirit reads 326 against 321 reserved, and the 4% is about 12 of that, so the five curses can't be paid without it on this gear. Node power doesn't count reserved Spirit as damage, so it would spend those points elsewhere.

b's Morior Invictus is a ready-made corrupted five-socket copy at 14 divines, where a plain copy has four: 11 Spirit and +52 life a socket, with five resistance runes. The 2-3 divine five-socket copies carry none of those lines and fail b's floor, so buy it with its lines, not the cheapest copy.

On b the cast speed just outruns the recharge: a full pool lasts about 500 seconds of unbroken casting with no hit taken, less when hits stop the recharge, so Eldritch Empowerment's 30% more holds through a normal fight.

Spiral into Insanity is b's anoint for both its lines. Against an empty anoint it read damage +2.5%, EHP +9.8% and lowest max hit +3.9%; Patient Barrier read no damage, EHP +9.3% and +8.4%, and Melding no damage, EHP +7.4% and +6.8%. Its recipe is in the record.

bootsException.reason: Windscream's "Curses have no Activation Delay" is what lets the bolts chain as a pack arrives; the build assumes it reaches Blasphemy's curses, which needs in-game testing, and without it each pack waits out the delay uncursed, at less than half the hit and no chain

groups.label: Coiling Bolts
groups.countReason: one cast fires a physical and a chaos projectile at once, and PoB rates each stat set alone; the two carry the same base damage and the same per-curse gains, so two copies of the rated bolt stand for the cast

engagement.reason: the bolts chain only through cursed monsters, and the curses reach about six metres around you, so the pack and the boss stand next to you while you cast

boss.note: Stand in the curse aura's reach and spam Coiling Bolts: both bolts hit, which the group's Count of 2 stands for, so the chaos bolt is the one entry. Nothing waits on a cooldown; Unleash's two Seals refill every few casts

earned.uptime: every spell cast with at least 5% of maximum energy shield left; the sacrifice doesn't interrupt recharge, but casting flat out it takes 14.2% of the pool a second against 12.5% recharged, so a full pool carries about a minute of unbroken casting, less when hits stop the recharge, and walking between packs gives it back
one Wither every 1.45 seconds on enemies in Presence, each lasting 7 seconds at 20% quality: 7 / 1.45 = 4 steady stacks on a boss; a pack that dies inside three seconds meets one or two
30 seconds stands for the middle of a one-minute boss fight, +15% more; it applies only to rare and unique enemies, and a rare that dies in seconds gets a few percent

claims.text: n's tree keeps Efficient Inscriptions and Zone of Control, for the same reasons as b: the first pays for the five curses, and the second widens the aura the chain runs in. Node power sees neither the reserved Spirit nor the chain.

n's tree keeps Enhanced Barrier, Mindful Awareness and Patient Barrier at the user's request: they are the design gate's first defence trade, taken over Pure Chaos and Wither Away, and they carry n's EHP to 19,823, inside its toughness band. Node power ranks by damage first, so a damage swap would spend them.

Upgrade from b in this order: Morior Invictus first at 80 divines, since it moves EHP most, then the gloves at 20 and belt at 16, the two sapphires at 5 each and the top rolls of Threaded Light, Veilpiercer and Windscream, then the amulet at 77 divines, whose listing leaves out the chaos line n's cap needs, so expect 100 to 200 for one with it. Against the Darkness comes last: 105 divines for +6.6% damage and no toughness, and Spirit stays paid without it.

claims.text: On n the cast speed outruns the recharge: casting flat out, Eldritch Empowerment's 5% a cast takes 14.2% of the pool a second against 12.5% recharged, so a full pool lasts about 57 seconds of unbroken casting with no hit taken. Every hit that stops the recharge shortens that, and the 30% more ends with the pool. On a long boss fight, stop casting to let it refill.

n's Morior Invictus is a corrupted five-socket copy, where a plain copy has four. It carries 14 Spirit, 11% global defences and +59 life per socket at 80 divines and gives up the all-resistance line, so three sockets hold resistance runes and the belt adds lightning resistance. Copies with Spirit, resistances and defences together cost 125 divines corrupted with four sockets, 500 uncorrupted with four, and 1 mirror with five.

The sapphires' maximum energy shield line is the desecrated hybrid with increased Spell Damage, which any jewel base rolls, so that line ties the jewel to no base; the plain spell damage and cast speed lines are what need a Diamond or Sapphire. The 10% increased Withered Magnitude line in the plan's text can't exist on the bought jewel: it is a third prefix beside the plain spell damage line and the hybrid, on a rare jewel that holds two. It reads 0 in PoB and the sapphires' prices don't require it, so buy them without it.
